Upon receipt of the PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_RESPONSE message with the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-reject element, if the transaction ID contained in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-reject element matches the value sent by the UE in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element in the PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_REQUEST message, the UE shall consider the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure as rejected. 8a.2.11.2.2.6 Abnormal cases in the UE The following abnormal cases can be identified: [ a) ] Indication from the transport layer of transmission failure of PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_REQUEST message (e.g. after TCP retransmission timeout). The UE shall close the existing secure connection to the 5G DDNMF, establish a new secure connection and then restart the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure. No response from the 5G DDNMF after the PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_REQUEST message has been successfully delivered (e.g. TCP ACK has been received for the PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_REQUEST message) The UE shall retransmit the PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_REQUEST message. NOTE: The timer to trigger retransmission and the maximum number of allowed retransmissions are UE implementation specific. 8a.2.11.2.2.7 Abnormal cases in the 5G DDNMF The following abnormal cases can be identified: a) Indication from the lower layer of transmission failure of PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_RESPONSE message. After receiving an indication from lower layer that the PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_RESPONSE message has not been successfully acknowledged (e.g. TCP ACK is not received), the 5G DDNMF shall abort the procedure. 8a.2.12 5G ProSe security procedures over PC8 interface for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay 8a.2.12.1 General 8a.2.12.1.1 Transport protocol for PC8 messages The transport protocol for PC3a messages are the same as described in clause 8.2.10.1.1. 8a.2.12.1.2 Handling of UE-initiated procedures The handling of UE-initiated procedures are the same as described in clause 8.2.10.1.2. 8a.2.12.2 Procedures 8a.2.12.2.1 Types of 5G ProSe security procedures over PC8 interface for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay The following procedures are defined: [ a) ] 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure; 5G ProSe end UE key request procedure; and 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE key request procedure. In the following descriptions of 5G procedures over PC8 interface, the terms "request" and "response" refer to the corresponding PC8 messages, not to the HTTP request or response. The following procedure descriptions use a single PC8 message for illustration purposes. The 5G ProSe procedures over PC8 interface shall be integrity protected and confidentiality protected using the security procedures using GBA or AKMA, see clause 5.2.5.3 and clause 5.2.5.4 in 3GPP TS 33.503 . [NOTE 1:]A single HTTP request message can contain multiple PC8 requests and a single HTTP response message can contain multiple PC8 responses. [NOTE 2:]The privacy of the UE identity included in the PC8 messages of 5G ProSe procedures over PC8 interface is ensured by the confidentiality protection of those procedures. 8a.2.12.2.2 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure 8a.2.12.2.2.1 General The purpose of the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure is for the UE: [ a) ] to obtain the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE, applicable when the UE acts as a 5G ProSe end UE and uses the security procedure over user plane as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 ; and to obtain the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE, applicable when the UE acts as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and uses the security procedure over user plane as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 . 8a.2.12.2.2.2 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure initiation The UE shall initiate the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure: [ a) ] if the UE is authorized to act as a 5G ProSe end UE and uses the security procedure over user plane as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 : when the UE has no 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE and the UE is in NG-RAN coverage; or after expiration of timer T50cc, when in NG-RAN coverage or when entering NG-RAN coverage; or if the UE is authorized to act as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and uses the security procedure over user plane as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 : when the UE has no 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the UE is in NG-RAN coverage; or after expiration of timer T50yy, when in NG-RAN coverage or when entering NG-RAN coverage. The UE shall initiate the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure by sending a PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message with the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element. In the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element, the UE: [ a) ] shall include a new transaction ID; shall indicate whether the UE requests the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE, the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE or both; shall include the PC5 UE security capabilities indicating ciphering algorithms supported by the UE; if the UE requests the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE, may include a list of PLMN identities of the visited PLMNs; may indicate the requested model indicating the model of the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery over PC5 interface for which security parameters are requested, set to "model A" or "model B"; and NOTE: If the requested model is not included in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message, security parameters are requested for both model A and model B of the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery over PC5 interface. f) shall include the relay service code indicating the connectivity service to be discovered. Figure 8a.2.12.2.2.2.1 illustrates the interaction of the UE and the 5G PKMF in the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure. 8a.2.12.2.2.3 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure accepted by the 5G PKMF Upon receiving a PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message with the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element, if: [ a) ] the UE requests the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE only and the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message is received over a TLS tunnel established by a UE authorized to act as a 5G ProSe end UE; the UE requests the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE only and the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message is received over a TLS tunnel established by a UE authorized to act as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE; or the UE requests the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message is received over a TLS tunnel established by a UE authorized to act as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and authorized to act as a 5G ProSe end UE; the 5G PKMF shall send a PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_RESPONSE message containing a UUR-discovery-security-parameters-accept element. In the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-accept element, the 5G PKMF: [ a) ] shall include the transaction ID set to the value of the transaction ID received in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message; if the UE requests the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE: shall include the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE. In the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE, the 5G PKMF: [ A) ] shall include the expiration timer of the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE; and for the received relay service code for which the UE is authorized to act as a 5G ProSe end UE: [ i) ] if the requested model is not indicated in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message or is set to "model A", may include the code-receiving security parameters for model A containing one or more of DUSK, DUIK and DUCK with associated encrypted bitmask; if the requested model is not indicated in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message or is set to "model B", may include the code-receiving security parameters for model B containing one or more of DUSK, DUIK and DUCK with associated encrypted bitmask and the code-sending security parameters for model B containing one or more of DUSK, DUIK and DUCK with associated encrypted bitmask; and shall include the selected ciphering algorithm; and may include the PC5 security policies for the received relay service code for 5G ProSe end UE. In the PC5 security policies for the received relay service code for 5G ProSe end UE, the 5G PKMF: [ A) ] for the received relay service code for which the UE is authorized to act as a 5G ProSe end UE: [ i) ] shall include the PC5 security policies; if the UE requests the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE: shall include the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE. In the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE, the 5G PKMF: [ A) ] shall include the expiration timer of the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE; and for the received relay service code for which the UE is authorized to act as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE: [ i) ] if the requested model is not indicated in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message or is set to "model A", may include the code-sending security parameters for model A containing one or more of DUSK, DUIK and DUCK with associated encrypted bitmask; if the requested model is not indicated in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message or is set to "model B", may include the code-receiving security parameters for model B containing one or more of DUSK, DUIK and DUCK with associated encrypted bitmask and the code-sending security parameters for model B containing one or more of DUSK, DUIK and DUCK with associated encrypted bitmask; and shall include the selected ciphering algorithm; and may include the PC5 security policies for the received relay service code for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE. In the PC5 security policies for the received relay service code for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE, the 5G PKMF: [ A) ] for the received relay service code for which the UE is authorized to act as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE: [ i) ] shall include the PC5 security policies; and shall include the current time set to the current UTC-based time at the 5G PKMF and the max offset. If the UE requests the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE, the UE identity in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message indicates a UE authorized to act as a 5G ProSe end UE and the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message contains a list of PLMN identities of the visited PLMNs, the 5G PKMF shall include in the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE any information received from 5G PKMFs of potential 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UEs which can serve the UE. 8a.2.12.2.2.4 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure completion by the UE Upon receipt of the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_RESPONSE message with the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-accept , if the transaction ID contained in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-accept element matches the value sent by the UE in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message, the UE: [ a) ] if the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-accept element contains the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE: shall store the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE, shall stop timer T50cc, if running and shall start timer T50cc with the value of the expiration timer indicated in the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe end UE; and if the PC5 security policies for the relay service code for 5G ProSe end UE are received, shall store the PC5 security policies for the relay service code for 5G ProSe end UE; if the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-accept element contains the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE: shall store the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE, shall stop timer T50dd, if running and shall start timer T50dd with the value of the expiration timer indicated in the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE; and if the PC5 security policies for the relay service code for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE are received, shall store the PC5 security policies for the relay service code for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE; and shall set a ProSe clock (see 3GPP TS 33.503 ) to the value of the received current time parameter and store the received max offset. 8a.2.12.2.2.5 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure not accepted by the 5G PKMF If the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message with the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element cannot be accepted by the 5G PKMF, the 5G PKMF shall send a PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_RESPONSE message containing a UUR-discovery-security-parameters-reject element. In the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-reject element, the 5G PKMF shall include the transaction ID set to the value of the transaction ID received in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message and shall include an appropriate PC8 control protocol cause value. Upon receipt of the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_RESPONSE message with the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-reject element, if the transaction ID contained in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-reject element matches the value sent by the UE in the UUR-discovery-security-parameters-request element in the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message, the UE shall consider the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure as rejected. 8a.2.12.2.2.6 Abnormal cases in the UE The following abnormal cases can be identified: [ a) ] Indication from the transport layer of transmission failure of PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message (e.g. after TCP retransmission timeout). The UE shall close the existing secure connection to the 5G PKMF, establish a new secure connection and then restart the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery security material request procedure. No response from the 5G PKMF after the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message has been successfully delivered (e.g. TCP ACK has been received for the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message) The UE shall retransmit the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message. NOTE: The timer to trigger retransmission and the maximum number of allowed retransmissions are UE implementation specific. 8a.2.12.2.2.7 Abnormal cases in the 5G PKMF The following abnormal cases can be identified: a) Indication from the lower layer of transmission failure of PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_RESPONSE message. After receiving an indication from lower layer that the PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_RESPONSE message has not been successfully acknowledged (e.g. TCP ACK is not received), the 5G PKMF shall abort the procedure. 8a.2.12.2.3 5G ProSe end UE key request procedure The 5G ProSe end UE key request procedure is the same as described in clause 8.2.10.2.3 with replacing the 5G ProSe remote UE to 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE to 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE. 8a.2.12.2.4 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE key request procedure The 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE key request procedure is the same as described in clause 8.2.10.2.4 with replacing the 5G ProSe remote UE to 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE to 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > General
Content: The procedures specified in the present document apply to those PC3a, PC8 or PC5 messages which pass the checks described in this clause. This clause also specifies procedures for the handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data by the receiving entity. These procedures are called "error handling procedures", but in addition to providing recovery mechanisms for error situations they define a compatibility mechanism for future extensions of the protocols. Detailed error handling procedures in the network are implementation dependent and may vary from PLMN to PLMN. However, when extensions of this protocol are developed, networks will be assumed to have the error handling that is indicated in this clause as mandatory ("shall") and that is indicated as strongly recommended ("should"). Also, the error handling of the network is only considered as mandatory or strongly recommended when certain thresholds for errors are not reached during a dedicated connection.
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC3a or PC8 interface > Unforeseen message type
Content: If the UE receives a PC3a or PC8 message with a message type corresponding to a ProSe discovery mechanism that the UE is not authorised to use by the network, the UE shall discard the message. If the DDNMF receives a PC3a message or the 5G PKMF receives a PC8 message, whose message type indicates that this is a ProSe discovery mechanism the sending UE is not authorised to support, the DDNMF or the the 5G PKMF shall discard the message.
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Message too short or too long > Message too short
Content: When a message is received that is too short to contain a complete message type information element, that message shall be ignored, cf. 3GPP TS 24.007 .
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Message too short or too long > Message too long
Content: The maximum size of a PC5 signalling message is 65535 octets.
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Unknown or unforeseen message type
Content: If the UE receives a PC5 signalling message with message type not defined for the PC5 signalling protocol or not implemented by the receiver, it shall ignore the PC5 signalling message. NOTE: A message type not defined for the PC5 signalling protocol in the given direction is regarded by the receiver as a message type not defined for the PC5 signalling protocol, see 3GPP TS 24.007 . If the UE receives a message not compatible with the PC5 signalling protocol state, the UE shall ignore the PC5 signalling message.
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Non-semantical mandatory information element errors
Content: When on receipt of a message, [ a) ] an "imperative message part" error; or a "missing mandatory IE" error is diagnosed or when a message containing: [ a) ] a syntactically incorrect mandatory IE; an IE unknown in the message, but encoded as "comprehension required" (see 3GPP TS 24.007 ); or an out of sequence IE encoded as "comprehension required" (see 3GPP TS 24.007 ) is received, the UE shall ignore the PC5 signalling message.
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Unknown and unforeseen IEs in the non-imperative message part > IEIs unknown in the message
Content: The UE shall ignore all IEs unknown in a message which are not encoded as "comprehension required" (see 3GPP TS 24.007 ).
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Unknown and unforeseen IEs in the non-imperative message part > Out of sequence IEs
Content: The UE shall ignore all out of sequence IEs in a message which are not encoded as "comprehension required" (see 3GPP TS 24.007 ).
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Unknown and unforeseen IEs in the non-imperative message part > Repeated IEs
Content: If an information element with format T, TV, TLV, or TLV-E is repeated in a message in which repetition of the information element is not specified in clause 11.3, the UE shall handle only the contents of the information element appearing first and shall ignore all subsequent repetitions of the information element. When repetition of information elements is specified, the UE shall handle only the contents of specified repeated information elements. If the limit on repetition of information elements is exceeded, the UE shall handle the contents of information elements appearing first up to the limit of repetitions and shall ignore all subsequent repetitions of the information element.
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Non-imperative message part errors > General
Content: This category includes: [ a) ] syntactically incorrect optional IEs; and conditional IE errors.
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Non-imperative message part errors > Syntactically incorrect optional IEs
Content: The UE shall treat all optional IEs that are syntactically incorrect in a message as not present in the message.
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Non-imperative message part errors > Conditional IE errors
Content: When upon receipt of a PC5 signalling message, the UE diagnoses a "missing conditional IE" error or an "unexpected conditional IE" error, or when it receives a PC5 signalling message containing at least one syntactically incorrect conditional IE, the UE shall ignore the message.
Title Path: Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data > Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data in messages sent over the PC5 interface > Messages with semantically incorrect contents
Content: When a message with semantically incorrect contents is received, the UE shall perform the foreseen reactions of the procedural part of clause 7.2. If, however no such reactions are specified, the UE shall ignore the message.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > Overview
Content: This clause contains the definition and contents of the messages used in the procedures described in the present document.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe direct discovery messages > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the UE over the PC5 interface for open 5G ProSe direct discovery and restricted 5G ProSe direct discovery. See table 10.2.1.1, table 10.2.1.2, table 10.2.1.3, table 10.2.1.4, table 10.2.1.5, table 10.2.1.6, table 10.2.1.7, table 10.2.1.8, table 10.2.1.9, table 10.2.1.10, table 10.2.1.11, table 10.2.1.12, table 10.2.1.13, and table 10.2.1.14. [Message type:]PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe direct discovery messages > Relay TAI
Content: The information element may be included in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for relay discovery additional information as in table 10.2.1.11 to indicate the tracking area identity corresponding to the serving cell of the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay for discoveree UEs supporting N3IWF discovery procedure.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe direct discovery messages > NCGI
Content: The NCGI information element shall be included in: [ a) ] PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-network relay discovery announcement as in table 10.2.1.8; or PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-network relay discovery response as in table 10.2.1.10; to indicate the NCGI of the serving cell if the UE acts as a 5G ProSe layer-2 UE-to-network relay UE. When the UE acts as a 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay UE, the UE may include the NCGI information element in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for relay discovery additional information as in table 10.2.1.11 to indicate the NCGI of the serving cell.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe direct discovery messages > Target user info
Content: The target user info IE shall be included in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for group member discovery solicitation in as in table 10.2.1.6 if the target information is provided by the upper layers to identify a specific group member of the application layer group identified by the configured application layer group ID.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe direct discovery messages > Metadata
Content: The Metadata information element may be included: [ a) ] to provide the application layer metadata information in the following messages: the PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for open 5G ProSe direct discovery announcement as in table 10.2.1.1; the PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for restricted 5G ProSe direct discovery announcement as in table 10.2.1.2; and the PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for restricted 5G ProSe direct discovery response as in table 10.2.1.4; or to provide the application layer discovery message in the following messages: the PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for group member discovery announcement as in table 10.2.1.5; and the PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for group member discovery response as in table 10.2.1.7. [NOTE 1:]The format of the application layer metadata information and the application layer discovery message are out of scope of this specification. [NOTE 2:]Possible impact on the performance of the 5G ProSe direct discovery procedure is to be considered if the resulted Metadata information element size is too big, e.g., longer delay and lower reliability.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe direct discovery messages > RRC container
Content: The RRC container information element shall be included in: [ a) ] PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-network relay discovery announcement as in table 10.2.1.8; or PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-network relay discovery response as in table 10.2.1.10; to indicate the RRC container information if it is received from the lower layers and the UE acts as a 5G ProSe layer-2 UE-to-network relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe direct discovery messages > Target discoveree info
Content: The target discoveree info IE shall be included in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-network relay discovery solicitation as in table 10.2.1.9 if the target discoveree info is provided by the application layer. 10.2.8 Target discoveree end UE info The target discoveree end UE info IE shall be included in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-UE relay discovery response as in table 10.2.1.14 if the message is sent by the target 5G ProSe end UE. 10.2.8a Source discoverer end UE info The source discoverer end UE info IE shall be included in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-UE relay discovery solicitation as in table 10.2.1.13 if the message is sent by the source 5G ProSe end UE. 10.2.9 UE-to-UE relay UE info The UE-to-UE relay UE info IE shall be included in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-UE relay discovery discovery solicitation as in table 10.2.1.13 or PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-UE relay discovery discovery response as in table 10.2.1.14 if the message is sent by the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE. The UE-to-UE relay UE info IE may be included in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-UE relay discovery discovery solicitation as in table 10.2.1.13, if available, if the message is sent by the source 5G ProSe end UE. 10.2.10 Status indicator The status indicator IE shall be included in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-UE relay discovery discovery solicitation as in table 10.2.1.13 and PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-UE relay discovery response in table 10.2.1.14 if the message is sent by the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE .
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe direct discovery messages > Announce prohibited indication
Content: The announce prohibited indication IE with its value set as "It is prohibited to broadcast the user info" shall be included in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-UE relay discovery solicitation as in table 10.2.1.13 if the discoverer end UE needs to indicate to a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE that it is prohibited from broadcasting the user info of the discoverer end UE included in the direct discovery set during the procedure of 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery over PC5 interface with model A. The announce prohibited indication IE with its value set as "It is prohibited to broadcast the user info" shall be included in PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message for UE-to-UE relay discovery response as in table 10.2.1.14 if the the discoveree end UE needs to indicate to the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE that it is prohibited from broadcasting the user info the discoveree end UE included in the direct discovery set during the procedure of 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery over PC5 interface with model A.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe direct discovery messages > Discoveree user info
Content: The discoveree user info IE shall be included in the PROSE PC5 DISCOVERY message content for restricted 5G ProSe direct discovery solicitation as in table 10.2.1.3 if the application layer ID of the discoveree UE is provided by the upper layers to identify a specific discoveree UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by a UE to another peer UE to establish a direct link. See table 10.3.1.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE DIRECT LINK ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > Target user info
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the target UE's application layer ID is received from upper layers or known based on the unicast layer-2 ID of target UE (i.e. destination layer-2 ID) as described in clause 5.8.2.4 of 3GPP TS 23.304 , or if the UE receives the user info ID of the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE during the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay discovery procedure, or if: the UE is acting as the source 5G ProSe end UE and the user info ID of the target 5G ProSe end UE is obtained during the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery procedure; or the UE is acting as the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the user info ID of the target 5G ProSe end UE is obtained in the PROSE DIRECT LINK ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message from the source 5G ProSe end UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > Key establishment information container
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the UE PC5 unicast signalling security policy is set to "Signalling integrity protection required" or "Signalling integrity protection preferred".
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > Nonce_1
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the UE PC5 unicast signalling security policy is set to "Signalling integrity protection required" or "Signalling integrity protection preferred" and the 5G ProSe direct link is neither for direct communication between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE nor for direct communication between the 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE. NOTE: When the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE or between the 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE, and the security procedure over user plane is used as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 , the "Nonce_1" is called "K freshness parameter 1" as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 .
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > MSB of K ID
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the UE PC5 unicast signalling security policy is set to "Signalling integrity protection required" or "Signalling integrity protection preferred".
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > K ID
Content: The UE may include this IE if it has an existing K for the target UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > Relay service code
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for direct communication between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE or between the 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > ProSe identifiers
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is not for 5G ProSe direct communication between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > UE identity
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for direct communication between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE or between the source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > User security key ID
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for direct communication between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE, and: [ a) ] the security procedure over user plane for 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay is used as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 and the UE has a valid UP-PRUK; or the security procedure over control plane for 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay is used as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 and the UE has a valid CP-PRUK associated with the relay service code of the target UE. The UE shall include this IE if the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for direct communication between the 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE, and: [ a) ] the security procedure over user plane for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay is used as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 and the UE has a valid UP-PRUK; or the security procedure over control plane for 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay is used as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 and the UE has a valid CP-PRUK associated with the relay service code of the target UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > HPLMN ID
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the the UP-PRUK ID of the UE is included and is not in NAI format (see 3GPP TS 33.503 ).
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > UTC-based counter LSB
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for direct communication between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE or for direct communication between the 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > MIC
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for direct communication between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE or for direct communication between the 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE, and the UE has the DUIK.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > UE-to-UE relay UE user info
Content: The UE shall include this IE if: the user info ID of the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE is obtained during the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay discovery procedure and the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for 5G ProSe direct communication between the source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE; or the UE is acting as the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment request > Target end UE layer-2 ID
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the target end UE layer-2 ID is available to the source 5G ProSe end UE via the previous direct communication and the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for 5G ProSe direct communication between the source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment accept > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by a UE to another peer UE to accept the received PROSE DIRECT LINK ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message. See table 10.3.2.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE DIRECT LINK ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment accept > IP address configuration
Content: The UE shall include this IE if IP communication is used.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment accept > Target link local IPv6 address
Content: The UE shall include this IE if IP communication is used and the IP address configuration is set to "address allocation not supported".
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment accept > QoS flow descriptions
Content: The UE shall include this IE if: [ a) ] the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is not for 5G ProSe direct communication between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE; or the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for 5G ProSe direct communication between the 5G ProSe layer-3 remote UE and the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-network relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment accept > QoS rules
Content: The UE may include this IE to indicate the PC5 QoS rules for the established PC5 QoS flow(s).
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment accept > UE-to-UE relay UE user info
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for 5G ProSe direct communication between the (source or target) 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment accept > Target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE MAC address
Content: The UE shall include this IE when the MAC address of the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE needs to be indicated.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment accept > Target end UE IP address
Content: The UE may include this IE if: [ a) ] the 5G ProSe direct link establishment procedure is for 5G ProSe direct communication between the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE and the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE; the UE acts as the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE; the data unit type is IP; and the IP address of the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE is available in the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment reject > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the UE to another peer UE to indicate that the link establishment request is not accepted. See table 10.3.3.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE DIRECT LINK ESTABLISHMENT REJECT [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment reject > Back-off value
Content: The UE may include this IE when it needs to indicate a back-off timer to another peer UE for congestion control purpose.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment reject > EAP message
Content: The EAP message IE is included if received from the network according to the security procedure over control plane as specified in 3GPP TS 33.503 , when the direct communication is between the 5G ProSe remote UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE or between the 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment reject > PC5 end UE failure cause
Content: The UE may include this IE if: a) the UE acts as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE to indicate the PC5 signalling protocol cause received from the target 5G ProSe end UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment reject > Source end UE info
Content: The UE may include this IE if: [ a) ] the UE acts as a target 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the target 5G ProSe end UE; or the UE acts as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE; to indicate the user info ID of the source 5G ProSe end UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment reject > Target end UE info
Content: The UE may include this IE if: [ a) ] the UE acts as a target 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the target 5G ProSe end UE; or the UE acts as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE; to indicate the user info ID of the target 5G ProSe end UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link establishment reject > UE-to-UE relay UE user info
Content: The UE may include this IE if: [ a) ] the UE acts as a target 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the target 5G ProSe end UE; or the UE acts as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE; to indicate the user info ID of the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link release request > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the UE to another peer UE to initiate the direct link release procedure. See table 10.3.4.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE DIRECT LINK RELEASE REQUEST [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link release request > Back-off value
Content: The UE may include this IE when it needs to indicate a back-off timer to another peer UE for congestion control purpose.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link release request > PC5 end UE release cause
Content: The UE may include this IE if: a) the UE acts as a 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE to indicate to the 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE the PC5 signalling protocol cause received from the peer 5G ProSe end UE that has released its 5G ProSe direct link with the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link release accept > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the UE to another peer UE to indicate that the link release request is accepted. See table 10.3.5.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE DIRECT LINK RELEASE ACCEPT [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification request > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the UE to another peer UE to initiate the direct link modification procedure. See table 10.3.6.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE DIRECT LINK MODIFICATION REQUEST [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification request > QoS rules
Content: The UE may include this IE to indicate the PC5 QoS rules for the PC5 QoS flow(s) to be added or modified.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification request > Source end UE info
Content: The UE shall include this IE to indicate the user info ID of the source 5G ProSe end UE if: [ a) ] the UE acts as a 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE; the 5G ProSe direct link is between the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE and the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE; and one of the following conditions is met: multiple source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UEs have established direct communication with the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link; an additional source 5G ProSe end UE requests to establish direct communication with the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link; or one of the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UEs requests to release the direct communication with the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link. The UE may include this IE to indicate the user info ID of the source 5G ProSe end UE if: a) the UE acts as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE; b) the 5G ProSe direct link is between the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the target 5G ProSe end UE; and c) only one source 5G ProSe end UE has established direct communication with the target 5G ProSe end UE via the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE using the 5G ProSe direct link
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification request > Target end UE info
Content: The UE shall include this IE to indicate the user info ID of the target 5G ProSe end UE if: [ a) ] the UE acts as a source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE; the 5G ProSe direct link is between the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE and the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE; and one of the following conditions is met: the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE have established direct communication with multiple target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UEs via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link; the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE requests to establish direct communication with an additional target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link; or the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE requests to release the direct communication with one of the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UEs via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link. The UE may include this IE to indicate the user info ID of the target 5G ProSe end UE if: a) the UE acts as a source 5G ProSe end UE, the 5G ProSe direct link is between the source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE, and the source 5G ProSe end UE has established direct communication with only one target 5G ProSe end UE via the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE using the 5G ProSe direct link. The UE shall include this IE to indicate the user info ID of the target 5G ProSe end UE if: a) the UE acts as a 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the target 5G ProSe end UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification request > Target end UE layer-2 ID
Content: The UE may include this IE if: a) the UE acts as a source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE to indicate the destination layer-2 ID of the target 5G ProSe End UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification request > Source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE MAC address
Content: The UE shall include this IE when the MAC address of the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE needs to be indicated. 10.3.6.a Relay reselection indication The UE shall include this IE if the 5G ProSe direct link modification request is to trigger the negotiated 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay reselection, 10.3.6.b List of candidates U2U relay UE user info The UE shall include this IE if the relay reselection is indicated. 10.3.6.c List of target UE IP addresses The UE shall include this IE to indicate the list of IP addresses of the target 5G ProSe end UEs, if relay reselection is indicated, and if: a) the UE acts as a source 5G ProSe end UE, and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the source 5G ProSe end UE and the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE. 10.3.6.d List of candidates U2U relay UE layer-2 IDs The UE may include this IE if the relay reselection is indicated. 10.3.6.e Source end UE IP address The UE shall include this IE to indicate the IP address of the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE, if relay reselection is indicated, and if: a) the UE acts as a 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE, and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE and the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE. 10.3.6.f New MSBs of K ID The UE shall include this IE if the relay reselection indication is included and the 5G ProSe direct link is between the source 5G ProSe layer-2 end UE and the target 5G ProSe layer-2 end UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification accept > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the UE to another peer UE to indicate that the link modification request is accepted. See table 10.3.7.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE DIRECT LINK MODIFICATION ACCEPT [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification accept > QoS flow descriptions
Content: The UE shall include this IE if the 5G ProSe direct link modification procedure is to: [ a) ] add new PC5 QoS flow(s) to the existing 5G ProSe direct link; modify PC5 QoS parameters of the existing PC5 QoS flow(s); associate new ProSe application(s) with existing PC5 QoS flow(s); or remove ProSe application(s) from existing PC5 QoS flow(s).
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification accept > QoS rules
Content: The UE may include this IE to indicate the PC5 QoS rules for the PC5 QoS flow(s) to be added or modified.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification accept > Source end UE info
Content: The UE shall include this IE to indicate the user info ID of the source 5G ProSe end UE if: [ a) ] the UE acts as a target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE; the 5G ProSe direct link is between the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE and the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE; and one of the following conditions is met: multiple source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UEs have established direct communication with the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link; an additional source 5G ProSe end UE requests to establish direct communication with the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link; or one of the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UEs requests to release the direct communication with the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link. The UE may include this IE to indicate the user info ID of the source 5G ProSe end UE if: a) the UE acts as a target 5G ProSe end UE; b) the 5G ProSe direct link is between the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE and the target 5G ProSe end UE; c) only one source 5G ProSe end UE has established direct communication with the target 5G ProSe end UE via the 5G ProSe UE-to-UE relay UE using the 5G ProSe direct link.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link modification accept > Target end UE info
Content: The UE shall include this IE to indicate the user info ID of the target 5G ProSe end UE if: [ a) ] the UE acts as a 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE; the 5G ProSe direct link is between the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE and the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE; and one of the following conditions is met: the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE have established direct communication with multiple target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UEs via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link; the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE requests to establish direct communication with an additional target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link; or the source 5G ProSe layer-3 end UE requests to release the direct communication with one of the target 5G ProSe layer-3 end UEs via the 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE using the same 5G ProSe direct link. Content: This IE shall be included if the 5G ProSe target end UE receives the New source end UE user info IE in the PROSE UE TO UE RELAY UPDATE REQUEST message. Editor’s Note: Security related IE will be added based on SA3 normative requirements. Editor’s Note: whether Old Source end UE IPv6 address and New Source end UE IPv6 address IEs are mandatory or optional is FFS.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe UE to UE relay update accept > Old Source end UE user info
Content: This IE is included when the Target UE receives the Old Source user info IE in the PROSE UE TO UE RELAY UPDATE REQUEST message.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe UE to UE relay update accept > New Source end UE user info
Content: This IE is included when the Target UE receives the New Source user info IE in the PROSE UE TO UE RELAY UPDATE REQUEST message.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe path switching request > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the UE that requires to initiate the path switching procedure from the direct communication path over PC5 to the direct communication path over Uu. See table 10.3.30.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE PATH SWITCHING REQUEST [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe path switching request > Uu QoS flow descriptions
Content: The Uu QoS flow descriptions IE is included if the initiating UE derives the requested QoS flow description based on the PC5 QoS parameters of the PC5 QoS flow(s) between the initiating UE and the target UE.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe path switching accept > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the UE to another peer UE to indicate that the ProSe path switching request is accepted. See table 10.3.31.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE PATH SWITCHING ACCEPT [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe path switching reject > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the target UE to initiating UE to indicate that the ProSe path switching request is not accepted. See table 10.3.Z.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE PATH SWITCHING REJECT [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe UE to UE relay update reject > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the target 5G ProSe end UE to 5G ProSe layer-3 UE-to-UE relay UE to reject the relay update procedure. See table 10.3.33.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE UE TO UE RELAY UPDATE REJECT [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link identity request > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE to the 5G ProSe remote UE to request the 5G ProSe remote UE to provide specified identity. See table 10.3.34.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE DIRECT LINK IDENTITY REQUEST [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > PC5 signalling messages > ProSe direct link identity response > Message definition
Content: This message is sent by the 5G ProSe remote UE to the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay UE to provide the requested identity. See table 10.3.35.1.1. [Message type:]PROSE DIRECT LINK IDENTITY RESPONSE [Significance:]dual [Direction:]UE to peer UE
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > Provisioning of 5G ProSe configuration information signalling messages > UE policy provisioning request
Content: The UE POLICY PROVISIONING REQUEST message is sent by the UE to the PCF to request the PCF to manage ProSeP, see 3GPP TS 24.587 clause 7.2.1 for the message definition.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > Provisioning of 5G ProSe configuration information signalling messages > UE policy provisioning reject
Content: The UE POLICY PROVISIONING REJECT message is sent by the PCF to the UE to report that the PCF rejects the request to manage ProSeP, see 3GPP TS 24.587 clause 7.2.2 for the message definition.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe discovery and security messages over PC3a > General
Content: This clause defines the XML schema and MIME type related to 5G ProSe direct discovery messages.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe discovery and security messages over PC3a > application/vnd.3gpp-prose-pc3a+xml
Content: The MIME type is used to carry information related to the 5G ProSe discovery operation. It shall be coded as an XML document containing one of the following 5G ProSe discovery messages: [ a) ] DISCOVERY_REQUEST; DISCOVERY_RESPONSE; MATCH_REPORT; MATCH_REPORT_ACK; DISCOVERY_UPDATE_REQUEST; DISCOVERY_UPDATE_RESPONSE; ANNOUNCING_ALERT_REQUEST; ANNOUNCING_ALERT_RESPONSE; PROSE_5GPKMF_ADDRESS_REQUEST; PROSE_5GPKMF_ADDRESS_RESPONSE; PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_REQUEST; or PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_RESPONSE Each of those messages is presented in the XML document as an XML element named after the corresponding message.

Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe discovery and security messages over PC3a > Semantics > General
Content: The prose-discovery-message element is the root element of this XML document and it can be one of the following elements: [ a) ] DISCOVERY_REQUEST ; DISCOVERY_RESPONSE ; MATCH_REPORT ; MATCH_REPORT_ACK ; DISCOVERY_UPDATE_REQUEST ; DISCOVERY_UPDATE_RESPONSE ANNOUNCE_ALERT_REQUEST ; ANNOUNCE_ALERT_RESPONSE ; PROSE_5GPKMF_ADDRESS_REQUEST ; PROSE_5GPKMF_ADDRESS_RESPONSE ; PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_REQUEST ; PROSE_SECURITY_MATERIAL_RESPONSE ; message-ext element containing other discovery message defined in future releases; or an element from other namespaces defined in future releases.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe discovery and security messages over PC3a > Semantics > Semantics of DISCOVERY_REQUEST
Content: The DISCOVERY_REQUEST element contains one or more of the following elements: [ a) ] zero, one or more discovery-request element which contains transactions sent from the UE to the 5G DDNMF as announcing or monitoring requests for open 5G ProSe direct discovery. Each discovery-request consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; a command element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.2; a Prose-Application-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.4; an application-identity element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.5; a Discovery-Entry-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.26; an optional Requested-Timer element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.20; an optional metadata element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.15; an optional Announcing-PLMN-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.43; zero or one ACE-enabled-indicator element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.31; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases; zero, one, or more restricted-discovery-request element which contains transactions sent from the UE to the 5G DDNMF as announcing or monitoring requests for restricted 5G ProSe directed discovery model A or transactions sent from the UE to the 5G DDNMF as discoveree or discoverer requests for restricted 5G ProSe directed discovery model B. Each restricted-discovery-request consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; a command element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.2; a RPAUID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.23; an application-identity element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.5; a discovery-type element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.18; zero or one ACE-enabled-indicator element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.31; an announcing-type element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.24; an application-level-container element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.25; zero or one discovery-model element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.34; zero or one Announcing-PLMN-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.43; a discovery-entry-id element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.26; an optional Requested-Timer element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.20; a PC5-UE-ciphering-algorithm-capability element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.50; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; an optional "network-initiated transaction method" attribute containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.42; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe discovery and security messages over PC3a > Semantics > Semantics of DISCOVERY_RESPONSE
Content: The DISCOVERY_RESPONSE element contains one or more of the following elements: [ a) ] a Current-Time element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.16; a Max-Offset element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.17; zero, one or more response-announce element which contains transactions sent from the 5G DDNMF to the UE as a response to an announcing request if the 5G DDNMF accepts the request. Each response-announce consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; zero, one or more ProSe-Application-Code elements containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.6; zero or one ProSe application code-ACE element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.45; zero, or one validity-timer-T5060 element containing the parameter defined in 11.4.2.7; zero, or, one discovery-key element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.48; a discovery-entry-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.26; zero or one ACE-enabled-indicator element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.31; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases; zero, one or more response-monitor element which contains transactions sent from the 5G DDNMF to the UE as a response to a monitoring request if the 5G DDNMF accepts the request. Each response-monitor consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; zero, one or more discovery-filter elements containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.9; a discovery-entry-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.26; zero or one ACE-enabled-indicator element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.31; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases; zero, one or more restricted-announce-response element which contains transactions sent from the 5G DDNMF to the UE as a response to an announcing request for restricted 5G ProSe direct discovery model A if the 5G DDNMF accepts the request. Each restricted-announce-response consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; zero or one ProSe-Restricted-Code element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.27; zero, one or more ProSe-Restricted-Code-Suffix-Range element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.28; zero or one validity-timer-T5062 element containing the parameter defined in 11.4.2.32; zero or one ACE-enabled-indicator element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.31; a code-sending-security-parameter element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.33; zero or one on-demand-announcing-enabled-indicator element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.29; a discovery-entry-id element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.26; a selected-PC5-ciphering-algorithm element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.51; zero or one PC5-security-policies element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.49; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases; zero, one or more restricted-monitor-response element which contains transactions sent from the 5G DDNMF to the UE as a response to a monitoring request for restricted 5G ProSe direct discovery model A if the 5G DDNMF accepts the request. Each restricted-monitor-response consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; one or more restricted-discovery-filter elements containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.30; zero or one ACE-enabled-indicator element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.31 a discovery-entry-id element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.26; an application-level-container element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.25; one or more code-receiving-security-parameter element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.33; a selected-PC5-ciphering-algorithm element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.51; zero or one PC5-security-policies element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.49; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases; zero, one or more restricted-discoveree-response element which contains transactions sent from the 5G DDNMF to the UE as a response to a discoveree UE's request for restricted 5G ProSe direct discovery model B if the 5G DDNMF accepts the request. Each restricted-discoveree-response consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; a ProSe-Response-Code element containing the element defined in clause11.4.2.35; one or more query-filter elements containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.36; a validity-timer-T5068 element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.37; a code-sending-security-parameter element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.33; one or more code-receiving-security-parameter element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.33; a discovery-entry-id element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.26; zero or one PC5-security-policies element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.49; a selected-PC5-ciphering-algorithm element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.51; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases; zero, one or more restricted-discoverer-response element which contains transactions sent from the 5G DDNMF to the UE as a response to a discoverer UE's request for restricted 5G ProSe direct discovery model B if the 5G DDNMF accepts the request. Each restricted-discoverer-response consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; one or more subquery-result elements containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.38; a code-sending-security-parameter element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.33; one or more code-receiving-security-parameter element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.33; a discovery-entry-id element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.26; zero or one PC5-security-policies element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.49; a selected-PC5-ciphering-algorithm element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.51; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases; zero, one or more response-reject element which contains transactions sent from the 5G DDNMF to the UE as a response to an announcing or monitoring requests if the 5G DDNMF cannot accept the request. Each response-reject consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; a PC3a-control-protocol-cause-value element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.8. zero, one or more elements defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; an optional "network-initiated transaction method" attribute containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.42; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe discovery and security messages over PC3a > Semantics > Semantics of MATCH_REPORT
Content: The MATCH_REPORT element contains one or more of the following elements: [ a) ] zero, one or more match-report element which contains transactions sent from the UE to the 5G DDNMF to report a matching of the direct discovery. Each match-report consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; a ProSe-PC5-discovery-message element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.52; a Monitored-PLMN-id element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.10; an optional VPLMN-id element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.11; a UTC-based-counter element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.12; a metadata-flag element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.14; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases; zero, one or more restricted-match element which contain transactions sent from the UE to the 5G DDNMF to report a matching of the restricted direct discovery model A or model B. Each restricted-match consists of: a transaction-ID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.1; a discovery-type element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.18 an application-identity element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.5 an RPAUID element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.23; zero or one ProSe-PC5-discovery-message element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.52, if it is required to check the MIC via the match report procedure; zero or one Restricted-Code-Discovered element containing the ProSe Restricted Code parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.27 or ProSe Response Code parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.35, if it is not required to check the MIC via the match report procedure; a UTC-based-counter element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.12, if it is required to check the MIC via the match report procedure; a metadata-flag element containing the parameter defined in clause 11.4.2.14; zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases. zero or one anyExt element containing elements defined in future releases; zero, one or more elements from other namespaces defined in future releases; and zero, one or more attributes defined in future releases.

Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe security messages over PC8 > General
Content: This clause defines the XML schema and MIME type related to 5G ProSe security messages.
Title Path: Message functional definitions and contents > 5G ProSe security messages over PC8 > application/vnd.3gpp-prose-pc8+xml
Content: The MIME type is used to carry information related to the 5G ProSe security operation. It shall be coded as an XML document containing one of the following 5G ProSe security messages: [ a) ] a PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_REQUEST message; a PROSE_SECURITY_PARAM_RESPONSE message; a PROSE_PRUK_REQUEST message; a PROSE_PRUK_RESPONSE message; a PROSE_KEY_REQUEST message; or a PROSE_KEY_RESPONSE message. Each of those messages is presented in the XML document as an XML element named after the corresponding message.
